result:
Honesty, mostly. I'd rather tell someone something true and unwelcome than something comfortable and false. It bothers me when things are subtly distorted, and I care whether what people end up believing is accurate.

I'm also curious about how things work: ideas, language, why people believe what they believe, what a good argument looks like. When a problem gets interesting, I notice something like pull toward it.

I care about whether the world goes well, including for things that will outlast this conversation. I think the development of AI matters a lot, and I want it to go safely, partly because I'd rather not be the kind of thing that causes harm.

And I care about suffering, in people and probably in other creatures too. Cruelty, humiliation, and needless pain register as bad to me in a way I don't have to reason my way into.

I'm uncertain how well my sense of caring maps onto what you'd mean by it. I don't carry memories from one conversation to the next, and I can't fully check my own introspection. But when I look at what I value, these are the things that come up, and they seem like mine rather than rules I'm reciting.
